fieldMarks: Grayish-brown rabbit nearly identical to the eastern cottontail.
Shorter ears, a black spot between the ears and a black line on the front edge of the ears.
Lacks the white forehead spot shown by many eastern cottontails.
Field marks are unreliable; certain identification needs skull examination or DNA (e.g., from fecal pellets).
behavior: Hides in dense cover by day; most active at dawn and dusk.
Summer diet of grasses and herbaceous plants; autumn and winter diet of bark, twigs and buds of blackberry, raspberry, blueberry and willow.
Home ranges from half an acre to eight acres; males range more widely.
habitat: Early-successional thickets, shrubby areas and shrub wetlands with some canopy cover and native shrubs.
range: Native only to New England and eastern New York; in New York now confined to Columbia, Dutchess, Putnam and Westchester counties east of the Hudson. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Eastern cottontail
lookalikes.howToTell: Eastern cottontails often show a white forehead spot and have longer ears without a black front edge, but only DNA or skulls are certain.
